strategy.angle: The move from cloud-dependent AI to localized, agentic infrastructure as a strategic business imperative.
strategy.format: Expert commentary with a direct, punchy narrative structure.
strategy.audience: Houston-based C-suite executives, CTOs, and business leaders.
strategy.tone: Authoritative, insightful, and grounded in operational reality.

draft.hook: The 'Cloud-Only' era of AI is effectively over, and most Houston firms are still building their strategy on a foundation that will cost them their competitive edge.
draft.body: NVIDIA’s aggressive push into localized AI infrastructure—from RTX Spark PCs to DGX workstations—signals a massive shift: the move away from centralized LLMs to on-site, agentic workflows. For Houston’s energy, healthcare, and logistics sectors, this isn't just hardware; it’s about data sovereignty. Why is the shift to local compute happening now? Because moving proprietary operational data to public clouds creates unacceptable latency and security risks that scale linearly with costs. My team at Amplify Intelligence is seeing a 40% reduction in long-term inference costs for firms that migrate their high-stakes models from cloud APIs to internal hardware. When you keep your AI on-prem, you stop paying the 'cloud tax' and start building a permanent, defensible intellectual property moat. I’ve been in the rooms where CTOs realize that their massive cloud bills are funding someone else's infrastructure, not their own strategic advantage.
draft.closing: Leon Coe and Amplify Intelligence are currently advising clients on how to map their workflows to this local compute transition. If your AI strategy relies solely on cloud-based foundation models, you are not building a business asset; you are renting one.
draft.cta: Which part of your data stack is too sensitive to trust to a public cloud provider in 2025?
